<solution_file path="src/t02_load_eurostat.py">
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# src/t02_load_eurostat.py
# This script reads the Eurostat sample data and writes the filtered indicator values
# for the selected indicators (see outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv) into
# outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv in RFC4180-compliant CSV format.
import json
import csv
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd


def main() -> None:
    # Paths
    config_path = Path("inputs/eurostat/sample_api_config.json")
    selected_indicators_path = Path("outputs/t01_selected_indicators.csv")
    output_path = Path("outputs/t02_eurostat_raw.csv")

    # Load the API configuration to find which CSV holds the data
    with open(config_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        api_cfg = json.load(f)

    base_path = api_cfg["base_path"]
    sample_df = pd.read_csv(base_path)

    # Read the list of indicator IDs we want to keep
    selected_df = pd.read_csv(selected_indicators_path)
    selected_ids = set(selected_df["indicator_id"].tolist())

    # Filter the sample dataframe
    filtered_df = sample_df[sample_df["indicator_id"].isin(selected_ids)].copy()

    # Ensure the expected columns; keep only those present
    columns = [
        "city_id",
        "city_name",
        "year",
        "indicator_id",
        "indicator_name",
        "value",
        "unit",
    ]
    filtered_df = filtered_df[columns]

    # Remove any duplicate rows (same city_id, year, indicator_id)
    filtered_df = filtered_df.drop_duplicates(subset=["city_id", "year", "indicator_id"])

    # Write the result with RFC4180 quoting
    filtered_df.to_csv(
        output_path,
        index=False,
        quoting=csv.QUOTE_MINIMAL,  # Quote only if needed
    )


if __name__ == "__main__":  # pragma: no cover
    main()
</solution_file>
